hero.heading: Shipping through uncertainty
hero.subheading: The 2026 Mid-Market Supply Chain Outlook: what 400 mid-sized manufacturers plan to change next year, and what they are holding back on.

image.alt: Illustration of a harbour at dusk with cranes loading shipping containers

themes.heading: Second sources, not new countries
themes.body: Most firms are not moving production. They are adding a backup supplier within the same region and paying a small premium for it.

themes.heading: Freight is the cost that surprised people
themes.body: Raw material prices settled in 2026. Freight did not, and few budgets had room for it.

themes.heading: Stock is back on the balance sheet
themes.body: Lean inventory is out of favour. Firms are holding more, and finance teams want to know what it costs.

image.alt: Illustration of warehouse shelving stacked with boxes

quote.text: Nobody we spoke to wants to rebuild their supply chain from scratch. They want one fallback for the parts that would stop the line.

faq.q: Who took part in the survey?
faq.a: 400 manufacturers with annual revenue between USD 50 million and USD 1 billion, across India, Southeast Asia and Europe.
